A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same preference-optimization work, renamed from Mallows-DPO to MallowsPO. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures, including image-only qualitative examples, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-bandit experiments, IMDB generation results, Pythia dialogue evaluations, and Llama3 fine-tuning results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds IPO/SimPO adaptation results and an ArmoRM-based dialogue evaluation.

M1.justification: The original theta/phi objectives, entropy-based dispersion proxy, and smoothing approximations are retained. Section 5.5 additionally applies dispersion to IPO and SimPO, introducing MallowsIPO and MallowsSimPO. These are limited procedural extensions; the MallowsPO renaming itself does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic bandits, IMDB, Anthropic HH, H4 Stack Exchange, SHP, UltraFeedback prompts, and AlpacaEval V2 for the same tasks. New evaluators and method comparisons retain this coverage. Replaced qualitative examples remain within SHP; curriculum learning and personalization are future directions only.

E2.justification: The Llama3 comparison expands from DPO alone to DPO, IPO, and SimPO, each compared with its dispersion-enhanced counterpart in v4 Table 1. IPO and SimPO were previously cited but not evaluated in this comparison, substantially broadening the comparator set.

E3.justification: Appendix F.1 adds an ArmoRM judging protocol for Pythia-2.8B at beta=0.1 alongside the retained GPT-4 evaluation. Table 1 introduces settings for IPO and SimPO comparisons. Existing training recipes, GPT-4 judging procedures, and the six DPO hyperparameter configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds an alternate-evaluator check of dialogue performance using ArmoRM. It also revises the qualitative case studies: four earlier examples are retained, two SHP examples are added, and eight earlier examples are removed, including all three DPO-winning cases. The six-setting hyperparameter analysis already existed in v2 Table 2.

E5.justification: v4 Table 1 explicitly reports per-metric standard deviations, including for retained DPO/Mallows scores. Figure 14 reports five runs and displays variability for the new ArmoRM evaluation. The ten-seed DPO/Mallows comparison was already present in v2; no increase in that run count is established.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial result entries: Table 1 reports LC win rates of 43.38% versus 44.73% for IPO/MallowsIPO and 50.04% versus 51.89% for SimPO/MallowsSimPO. Figure 14 adds approximately 69%, 55%, and 52% ArmoRM win rates on HH, SHP, and SE. These use a different evaluator from the retained GPT-4 results. Existing benchmark scores and the six-setting DPO grid are retained, while qualitative findings are added and removed.

T1.justification: v2 directly asserts the Mallows-theta logistic pairwise relationship. v4 instead introduces an assumed pairwise construction, Proposition 1, and a proof sketch connecting it to the full-ranking distribution, while distinguishing theta/phi consistency. Appendix B expands derivations, and Appendix C adds an item-count argument and a counterexample showing that the discrepancy functions order rankings differently. This exceeds theorem renumbering or restatement.

C1.justification: The central claims about dispersion-aware preference optimization and generalization remain. The abstract adds compatibility with other offline preference-optimization methods and nearly two percentage points of additional LC win rate. Combining dispersion with other objectives changes from a v2 future question to a reported contribution.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive discussion of curriculum learning and user-dependent dispersion for personalized alignment, explicitly reserving both for future work. Its conclusion newly identifies more accurate dispersion approximation as unresolved. Conversely, the qualitative discussion drops qualifications acknowledging cases where DPO produced more specific or preferable responses.

D1.justification: v4 adds a project-code access link, clarifies sequence-space normalization as n=k^N, and supplies beta/learning-rate settings for the new comparisons. Existing optimizer, batch-size, warmup, bandit-training, and GPT-4 judging details are retained in the relocated experimental appendix. The PDFs do not establish fuller implementation details for the new adaptations.

R1.justification: v4 adds the Winata survey, SHP/Stack Exchange source references, and curriculum-learning and personalized-alignment literature. It removes the Song et al. preference-ranking reference. These extend supporting context and future positioning, while the central relationship to Mallows ranking, Bradley-Terry, DPO, and generalized preference optimization remains.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming the method, v4 substantially restructures the exposition: preliminaries are compressed, Section 3.2 becomes theorem-led, smoothing moves to Appendix C.5, and the method comparison and hyperparameter grid move into appendices. The appendix organization expands and the experimental and concluding narratives are rewritten.

P2.justification: v4 adopts the ICLR layout, merges the bandit and IMDB frontier displays, relocates existing figures and tables, and adds ranking-distribution illustrations, the expanded comparison table, and ArmoRM plots. Qualitative examples become colored raster figures instead of text tables. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: The IPO/SimPO comparisons address v2's explicit open question about benefiting other objectives, and ArmoRM adds evidence beyond a single dialogue judge. Together with additional uncertainty reporting and code-access information, these strengthen the empirical case. The gain is limited by sparse adaptation details, removal of all three DPO-winning qualitative cases, and a new mathematical inconsistency: Section 3.1 gives distance 4 for a reversed ranking, while Appendix C Table 4 gives 8.
